Investigated: pdf-inspector's main branch already has the fix (commit 1c32e4bd, bumps lopdf to 0.42.0) but it was never published as a new crates.io release (last published 0.1.7, 2026-07-31, predates the fix). Then ran anydoc's own pre-built cargo-fuzz targets (all 8 formats, seeded from tests/fixtures/, ~90s each): csv/doc/rtf/ppt/docx/odf/epub/pdf clean, 0 crashes across ~1-3.5M execs each. xlsx crashed within seconds: 'attempt to multiply with overflow' in a transitive dependency (calamine 0.36.1), not anydoc's own code — see the calamine entry below. Not a scan target — reached transitively while fuzzing firecrawl/anydoc's xlsx cargo-fuzz target (seeded from anydoc's own test fixtures). Crash: 'attempt to multiply with overflow' at calamine-0.36.1/src/xlsx/mod.rs:2837, in get_row_and_optional_column (backs get_dimension/get_row_column/get_row — worksheet-dimension and merged-region parsing), reached via anydoc::formats::sheet::merged_regions parsing a crafted xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml. Root cause: the base-26 column and base-10 row accumulation loops used raw `*`/`+` with no length or bounds check, so an implausibly long letter/digit run (~20 chars) overflows u32 during accumulation and panics — before any bounds check gets a chance to run. A sibling parser in the same file (Reference::parse, used for cell-offset/range operations) already guards the identical input class correctly via wrapping_mul/wrapping_add + a post-hoc validate() against MAX_COLUMNS/MAX_ROWS; this function just never got the same protection, and its own callers don't do a follow-up bounds check the way Reference's constructors do. No PVR/SECURITY.md on the repo, but this is DoS-only (Rust panics safely, no memory corruption) with an obvious, minimal, convention-matching fix, so — per the same public-channel logic as an already-disclosed dependency CVE — fixed it directly rather than just filing a report: forked, patched both accumulation loops to checked_mul/checked_add returning the existing ColumnNumberOverflow/RowNumberOverflow errors (already defined and used by the sibling parser, no new error variant needed), added a regression test reproducing the exact crash plus the get_dimension call-path case, verified `cargo test --lib` (43 passed) and `cargo clippy --lib -- -D warnings` clean, opened tafia/calamine#705. The other 7 seeded anydoc fuzz targets (rtf, ppt, csv, docx, odf, epub, pdf; ~90s each) stayed clean throughout, 0 crashes — xlsx was the only one that turned up anything. Verified the fix locally end-to-end: patched anydoc's fuzz/Cargo.toml with a [patch.crates-io] path override to the fixed calamine fork (the override has to go in fuzz/Cargo.toml specifically — cargo-fuzz's fuzz/ directory has its own separate Cargo.lock, so a patch on the parent anydoc/Cargo.toml silently has no effect), ran `cargo update -p calamine` to pick it up, rebuilt, and re-ran the exact saved crash artifact: clean exit, no panic.
